## CodeQL / Incomplete URL substring sanitization

'[https://us-east-1.account.example.com](1)' may be followed by an arbitrary host name.

[Show more details](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/security/code-scanning/26)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify Apple form_post ID tokens**

When Apple callbacks arrive via `response_mode=form_post`, this path trusts `parseIdTokenClaims(idToken)` without verifying the JWT signature, issuer, or audience. An attacker who starts an Apple flow can see the state/nonce used for that flow and POST a forged unsigned/token payload with that nonce and any `sub`/`email`, causing AuthFn to link or create a session for the forged identity; use the same `jwtVerify`/audience checks as the native Apple path before accepting these claims.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Wrong fallback field for `regionId`. `item.SK` is always the constant sort-key string `'LOOKUP'` (defined as `LOOKUP_RECORD_SORT_KEY`), never a region ID. If a record lacks the `regionId` attribute (e.g. legacy data or a partial write), this silently returns `'LOOKUP'` as the region ID instead of failing with a clear error, corrupting all subsequent region-routing decisions for that identifier. ```suggestion regionId: readString(item.regionId, 'regionId'), ```

Path: authfn/adapters/lookup-dynamodb/src/index.ts Line: 180 Comment: Wrong fallback field for `regionId`. `item.SK` is always the constant sort-key string `'LOOKUP'` (defined as `LOOKUP_RECORD_SORT_KEY`), never a region ID. If a record lacks the `regionId` attribute (e.g. legacy data or a partial write), this silently returns `'LOOKUP'` as the region ID instead of failing with a clear error, corrupting all subsequent region-routing decisions for that identifier. ```suggestion regionId: readString(item.regionId, 'regionId'), ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````

Dead `AUTHFN_REGION_NOT_FOUND` branch. The server-side `buildLookupResult` was changed in this PR to return `{ continueLocally: true, ... }` instead of throwing `AuthFnRegionNotFoundError` when no region is found. The lookup endpoint now always returns HTTP 200, so `lookup.ok` is always `true` and this error-code branch is never entered. Prompt To Fix With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: authfn/client/src/regional-client.ts Line: 61-67 Comment: Dead `AUTHFN_REGION_NOT_FOUND` branch. _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Cache expiration inconsistency in region mismatch handling.**

Line 357 uses `DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL_MS` when constructing a cached region from a mismatch error. However, the user may have configured a different `cacheTtlMs` via `AuthFnRegionalClientOptions`. This creates inconsistent cache expiration: regions resolved from mismatches expire after 15 minutes, while explicitly looked-up regions expire according to the configured TTL.

Consider passing `cacheTtlMs` to `regionFromMismatch` or adjusting the expiration in the caller (`saveRegion` already updates expiry).




<details>
<summary>♻️ Proposed fix to use configured TTL</summary>

Update `regionFromMismatch` to accept `cacheTtlMs`:

```diff
 function regionFromMismatch(
   identifier: string,
-  response: unknown
+  response: unknown,
+  cacheTtlMs: number
 ): AuthFnCachedRegion | null {
   // ... existing validation logic ...
   
   return {
     identifier,
     regionId,
     authority,
     domain: typeof details.domain === 'string' ? details.domain : undefined,
     cachedAt: Date.now(),
-    expiresAt: Date.now() + DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL_MS
+    expiresAt: Date.now() + cacheTtlMs
   };
 }
```

Then update all call sites to pass `cacheTtlMs`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```

rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

regionFromMismatch function hardcodes DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL_MS causing mismatched
expiry; change regionFromMismatch to accept a cacheTtlMs parameter and use that
for expiresAt instead of DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL_MS, then update all call sites (e.g.,
where regionFromMismatch is invoked before saveRegion) to pass the configured
AuthFnRegionalClientOptions.cacheTtlMs so regions derived from
AUTHFN_REGION_MISMATCH use the same TTL as explicit lookups.
```

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Treat existing lookup records as idempotent, not automatic conflicts.**

`putIfAbsent()` returns `existing` on every repeat registration, and this branch throws without checking whether that record already belongs to `input.user.id`. After the first successful registration, later `registerUserRegion()` calls for the same identifier will start failing whenever `lookupStore` is enabled. Accept/update same-user mappings and only raise `AuthFnRegionMismatchError` when the stored record points at a different user or region. This also leaves `region_profiles` updated locally before the throw, so the two stores can diverge on the failure path.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```

In `@authfn/core/src/core/regions.ts` around lines 372 - 406, The current branch
that handles pluginConfig.lookupStore.putIfAbsent treats any returned existing
record as an automatic conflict; change registerUserRegion logic so that when
result.existing exists you first compare result.existing.userId and
region/authority with input.user.id and the new record: if the existing record
belongs to the same user (existing.userId === input.user.id) treat it as
idempotent and accept/update the lookup/cache (use lookupFromRecord and
setCachedJson as currently done) and do not emit a conflict event or throw
AuthFnRegionMismatchError; only emit emitAuthEvent and throw
AuthFnRegionMismatchError when the stored record points to a different user or a
different region/authority, and ensure you only update local region_profiles
after confirming no conflict to avoid diverging stores.
```

```ts
function sanitizeErrorDetails(input: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {
  if (!isRecord(input)) return undefined;
  const redactedKeys = new Set(['email', 'identifier', 'token', 'secret', 'code', 'authorization']);
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(input)) {
    out[key] = redactedKeys.has(key.toLowerCase()) ? '[redacted]' : value;
  }
  return out;
}
```
